title: Throat sounds and ts: ח ט צ ץ
why: Four more letters: ח, ט and the ts (צ ץ). It's time to take stock of the letters that sound the same, and to greet people depending on the time of day with טוֹב, which you can finally read in full.

The throat and the ts: ח, ט, צ, ץ

LetterNameSound
חkhetkh, like כ without a dot
טtett, like ת
צtsadits
ץfinal tsadits, at the end of a word

Don't confuse ח and ה: in ה, the left leg doesn't touch the roof; in ח, it does.

לֶחֶםlekhem: bread
עֵץets: tree

In English, the ts sound only shows up in the middle or at the end of a word (\"cats\", \"pizza\"); in Hebrew, it's common, even at the start of a word: צִ = tsi.

", "

Letters that sound the same

SoundLettersExamples
khח כ ךחָלָב khalav, מֶלֶךְ melekh
tט תטוֹב tov, תּוֹדָה toda
kק כּקָר kar, כֶּלֶב kelev
silentא עאֶרֶץ erets, עֵץ ets
vב ותֵּל אָבִיב, דָּוִד
sס (and soon שׂ)סוּס sus

When speaking, there's no difference at all. When writing, you have to know which letter to use: it's like the f sound in English, spelled \"f\" in \"fan\" but \"ph\" in \"phone\". Learn each word with its spelling.

Under ח or ע, the shva often becomes a small a (hataf patah): חֲבֵרָה (khavera, friend, f.), the feminine of חָבֵר (khaver).

", "

Good morning, good evening, good night

טוֹב (good), which you've recognized since the first lesson, is finally fully readable. It's used to greet people depending on the time of day:

בֹּקֶר טוֹב! — בֹּקֶר אוֹר!Good morning! — Good morning! (in the morning; the reply means \"morning of light\") [boker tov! — boker or!]
עֶרֶב טוֹבgood evening [erev tov]
לַיְלָה טוֹבgood night [layla tov]

The adjective agrees: לֶחֶם טוֹב (good bread), חֲבֵרָה טוֹבָה (a good friend, f.). At the table, people say בְּתֵאָבוֹן! (enjoy your meal!); \"on the table\" is עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן.

לַיְלָה (night) is masculine despite its final a: you say לַיְלָה טוֹב, never \"tova\".
